phase2: Tu croyais que c'était a piece of cake ? Attends, je n'ai pas encore sorti tous mes masques !
Arrêtons de tourner autour du pot : la phase deux commence, et the ball is in your court !
Tu as brisé la glace, bravo. Maintenant, on passe aux choses sérieuses.
phase3: Ça, c'est la goutte qui fait déborder le vase… the last straw ! Je sors le grand jeu !
Mon masque glisse… mais moi, je n'aurai pas la frousse au dernier moment !
Assez ri ! Tu vas te retrouver in hot water, comme on dit chez moi !
lose: Tu t'es dégonflé au dernier moment, hein ? Get cold feet, ça arrive aux meilleurs !
Allez, va te coucher (hit the sack, comme on dit) et reviens plus en forme demain.
Ne t'en fais pas : cette défaite est peut-être a blessing in disguise. Si tu avais gagné, tu n'aurais rien appris !

questions.q: If the referee ___ that goal, we would be in the final right now.
questions.explain: Conditionnel mixte : une condition passée (if + past perfect) avec un résultat présent (would be… right now).

questions.q: Comment dit-on « J'aurais aimé ne pas avoir vendu ma vieille guitare » ?
choices: I wish I didn't sell my old guitar.
I wish I wouldn't have sold my old guitar.
If only I haven't sold my old guitar.
I wish I hadn't sold my old guitar.
questions.explain: Regret sur le passé : wish + past perfect (hadn't sold). Jamais would après wish pour parler de soi.

questions.q: I'd have picked you up at the airport if you ___ me your flight number.
questions.explain: Troisième conditionnel : if + past perfect (had sent). Le 'd de I'd have = would ; jamais would dans la partie if.

questions.q: Luckily, the forecast warned us about the storm; ___, we would have been stuck on the lake.
questions.explain: Otherwise = sinon (si ça ne s'était pas passé ainsi). Il introduit le résultat imaginaire : we would have been stuck.

questions.lead: I didn't know you were vegetarian, so I made chicken.
questions.q: If I ___ vegetarian, I wouldn't have made chicken.
questions.explain: Troisième conditionnel : if + had + participe passé (had known), puis would have + participe.

questions.q: If you hadn't spilled coffee on my laptop, I ___ to buy a new one now.
questions.explain: Conditionnel mixte : condition passée (hadn't spilled), conséquence maintenant (now) : would + verbe de base, wouldn't have to.

questions.q: If only we ___ the weather forecast before the canoe trip!
questions.explain: If only + past perfect = regret sur le passé (si seulement nous avions vérifié).

questions.q: We ___ the last train if the taxi driver hadn't taken a shortcut.
questions.explain: Troisième conditionnel : would (might, could) have + participe passé dans la partie résultat.

questions.q: If Maya had accepted that job in Calgary, she ___ in Ottawa today.
questions.explain: Conditionnel mixte : choix passé (had accepted), situation présente (today) : wouldn't + verbe de base.

questions.q: If the team had trained harder, they would won the cup.
questions.explain: Troisième conditionnel : would have + participe passé. Il manque have : would have won.

questions.q: I wish I didn't shout at my brother yesterday.
questions.explain: Regret sur hier (passé) : wish + past perfect, I wish I hadn't shouted.

questions.q: If we hadn't taken the wrong exit, we would have arrive in time for the fireworks.
questions.explain: Après would have, il faut le participe passé : arrived.

questions.q: If I had gone to bed earlier, I won't be so tired now.
questions.explain: Conditionnel mixte (passé → présent) : le résultat imaginaire prend would, pas will : I wouldn't be so tired now.

questions.q: The lights are off and nobody's answering. They ___ to bed already.
questions.explain: Déduction presque sûre sur le passé : must have + participe passé.

questions.q: You ___ that email to the whole office! Now everyone knows about the surprise party.
questions.explain: Reproche : c'était une erreur, donc shouldn't have + participe. Can't have et might not have contredisent le fait que tout le monde le sait.

questions.q: « Elle a dû prendre un taxi : sa voiture était en panne. » (C'était une obligation.)
choices: She must have taken a taxi because her car had broken down.
She must take a taxi because her car had broken down.
She should have taken a taxi because her car had broken down.
She had to take a taxi because her car had broken down.
questions.explain: « A dû » = obligation passée : had to. Must have taken serait une supposition.

questions.q: Thank you for the flowers! You really ___ bought me anything, though.
questions.explain: Tu as acheté des fleurs alors que ce n'était pas nécessaire : needn't have + participe passé.

questions.q: There's flour all over the kitchen floor. The kids ___ cookies while we were out.
questions.explain: La farine est une preuve : déduction presque certaine sur le passé, must have made.

questions.q: Liam ___ the Montreal marathon last Sunday; he was at my place all day!
questions.explain: Déduction négative (impossible) : can't have ou couldn't have + participe. Run → run.

questions.q: The meeting was cancelled, so I ___ up at six. I could have slept in!
questions.hint: get, inutile mais je l'ai fait
questions.explain: Je me suis levé pour rien : needn't have + participe passé (got, ou gotten en anglais nord-américain).

questions.q: I'm not sure why Priya is late. She ___ the bus.
questions.explain: Possibilité dans le passé : might (may, could) have + participe passé.

questions.q: You ___ me you were coming! I would have cleaned the house.
questions.explain: Reproche sur le passé (tu aurais dû) : should have + participe passé, told.

questions.q: My phone isn't in my bag. I must of left it at the restaurant.
questions.explain: On entend « must of » à l'oral (must've), mais on écrit toujours must have.

questions.q: He can't have wrote this essay himself; it's far too good.
questions.explain: Modal + have + participe passé : can't have written (write, wrote, written).

questions.q: You should have saw the look on her face!
questions.explain: Après should have, il faut le participe passé : seen (see, saw, seen).

questions.q: The thief could have entered through the window; it was locked from the inside.
questions.explain: La fenêtre était verrouillée de l'intérieur : c'est impossible, donc couldn't have (ou can't have) entered.

questions.q: I hated losing my old job, but it turned out to be ___: my new one is much better.
questions.explain: A blessing in disguise = un mal pour un bien : une mauvaise chose qui finit par être positive.

questions.q: Comment dit-on « Arrête de tourner autour du pot ! » ?
questions.explain: Tourner autour du pot = beat around the bush (battre autour du buisson).

questions.q: The plumber worked for twenty minutes and charged us four hundred dollars. That repair ___!
choices: cost an arm and a leg
questions.explain: Cost an arm and a leg = coûter les yeux de la tête, être très cher.

questions.q: If Mom finds out you borrowed her car without asking, you'll be ___.
questions.explain: In hot water = dans le pétrin, avoir des ennuis.

questions.q: My brother promised to keep the surprise a secret, but he ___ the beans at breakfast.
questions.explain: Spill the beans = vendre la mèche. Le verbe se conjugue : au passé, spilled.

questions.q: Two days before the skydiving trip, Dad ___ cold feet and stayed home.
questions.explain: Get cold feet = se dégonfler au dernier moment. Au passé : got cold feet.

questions.q: Setting up the printer isn't rocket ___; just follow the instructions.
questions.explain: It's not rocket science = ce n'est pas sorcier, c'est simple. L'expression est figée.

questions.q: We've been painting since eight this morning. Let's ___ it a day.
questions.explain: Call it a day = arrêter de travailler pour aujourd'hui.

questions.q: Could you keep an eye ___ the soup while I answer the door?
questions.explain: Keep an eye on something = surveiller, garder un œil sur.

questions.q: Our neighbours from Vancouver visit us once in a red moon.
questions.explain: Très rarement = once in a blue moon. On ne change aucun mot d'une expression figée.

questions.q: I'm exhausted; I'm going to hit the bag.
questions.explain: Aller se coucher = hit the sack, pas the bag.

questions.q: The manager broke the glass with a joke at the start of the meeting.
questions.explain: Briser la glace = break the ice. Break the glass voudrait dire casser un verre !

questions.q: Stop pulling my arm! I know you didn't really win the lottery.
questions.explain: Faire marcher quelqu'un, le taquiner = pull someone's leg.

questions.q: The instructions were so confusing that half the class ___ the assignment.
questions.explain: Mis- = mal : misunderstand (mal comprendre). Au passé : misunderstood.

questions.q: Our bus driver works ___ hours: sometimes mornings, sometimes nights.
questions.explain: Devant un r, le préfixe négatif devient ir- : irregular.

questions.q: Her endless ___ makes her a brilliant scientist.
questions.explain: Curious + -ity = curiosity : le u de -ous disparaît (comme dans generosity).

questions.q: These pants are too long. Could you ___ them a little?
questions.explain: Le suffixe -en transforme un adjectif en verbe : short → shorten (raccourcir).

questions.q: The sudden ___ of a moose on the road made everyone scream.
questions.explain: Après the sudden, il faut un nom : appear + -ance = appearance.

questions.q: I think the hotel ___ us: the bill is twice the price we agreed on.
questions.explain: Over- = trop : overcharge = faire payer trop cher. Au passé : overcharged.

questions.q: Your argument is completely ___: the second point contradicts the first.
questions.explain: Devant un l, le préfixe négatif devient il- : illogical.

questions.q: We moved to a quieter ___ near the river.
questions.explain: Le suffixe -hood forme un nom : neighbour → neighbourhood (le quartier).

questions.q: My phone is completely ___ without a charger.
questions.explain: -less = sans : useless = sans utilité, inutile.

questions.q: The waiter was very unhelpfull, so we left.
questions.explain: Le suffixe -ful n'a qu'un seul l : unhelpful.

questions.q: Stop being so inmature and apologize to your sister.
questions.explain: Devant un m, le préfixe in- devient im- : immature.

questions.q: There's been a real improvment in your pronunciation.
questions.explain: Devant -ment, le e final reste : improve → improvement.

questions.q: Nobody realized the dangerosity of the situation.
questions.explain: « Dangerosité » est un mot français : dangerosity n'existe pas en anglais. On dit the danger of the situation.

questions.q: « On va au travail en autobus. » → We go to work ___.
questions.explain: Moyen de transport : by + nom, sans article (by bus, by car, by train).

questions.q: There's ___ milk left, so we can still make pancakes.
questions.explain: Milk est indénombrable, donc little / a little. A little = un peu (assez) ; little seul = presque pas (sens négatif).

questions.q: I asked both my parents for a ride, but ___ of them could drive me.
questions.explain: Deux personnes et un sens négatif (aucun des deux) : neither. None s'utilise pour plus de deux.

questions.q: ___ of my five roommates remembered to buy toilet paper.
questions.explain: Aucun parmi plus de deux = none of. Neither ne s'utilise que pour deux.

questions.q: Volunteers deliver hot meals to ___ every winter.
questions.explain: The + adjectif désigne un groupe de personnes : the homeless (les sans-abri), sans -s.

questions.q: My little brother ate the ___ pizza by himself!
questions.explain: Toute la pizza, la pizza entière = the whole pizza (the + whole + nom singulier).

questions.q: We have a few time before the train leaves; let's grab a coffee.
questions.explain: Time (le temps) est indénombrable : a little time, pas a few (réservé aux dénombrables).

questions.q: You can take either buses; they both go downtown.
questions.explain: Either (l'un ou l'autre) est suivi d'un nom au singulier : either bus.
